title: Summit Mileage Inactivity, Dormancy and Forfeiture
content:
In the Crestline Summit Loyalty Program, award miles can expire through inactivity only at a tier whose miles can expire.

**Rule.** When the member's tier is one whose miles can expire through inactivity and the whole calendar months elapsed since the latest qualifying activity reach the tier's inactivity months before expiry, the membership becomes dormant and its entire mile balance is forfeited, with inactivity as the ground of the forfeiture.

**Counting inactivity.** The count runs from the latest activity date on the membership to the handling date, in whole calendar months. Qualifying activity is any accrual, retro credit, partner accrual, purchase, transfer in or out, or redemption posting. Goodwill, bonus, reversal and forfeiture postings never count as activity and never keep miles alive.

**Elite tiers.** Members of every elite tier have miles that do not expire, so their miles never expire while they hold that tier; the clock applies again from the day a member falls to Summit Member.

**Forfeiture entry.** A forfeiture entry is booked only on a membership whose status is dormant or closed.

**Afterwards.** Any later qualifying activity makes a dormant membership active again, but forfeited miles return only through reinstatement. Qualifying dollars and upgrade certificates are not affected by dormancy.

### Whole-month boundary (hypothetical, a 24-month period)

| Latest qualifying activity | Handling date | Whole months elapsed | Period reached |
|---|---|---|---|
| 15 May 2023 | 14 May 2025 | 23 | No |
| 15 May 2023 | 15 May 2025 | 24 | Yes |

### Points of judgement

- A goodwill credit posted a month ago leaves the count running from the latest qualifying activity before it.
- A Summit Silver member's miles do not expire while Summit Silver is held, whatever the count shows.
- A dormant membership that receives a new flight accrual becomes active; the miles forfeited earlier stay forfeited unless reinstated.
